οἶνος, ἀκόλαστος ἄρα ὁ θυμὸς, ἀκολάστους ποιῶν τοὺς ἀνθρώπους· καὶ ὑβριστικὸν ἡ
ὀργή· γίνεται γὰρ ἀπὸ ζέοντος θυμοῦ· εἰ δὲ οἴνου οἱ Ναζαραῖοι κατὰ τὸν νόμον
ἀπέχονται, θυμοῦ ἄρα τοὺς Ναζαραίους ἐκτὸς εἶναι νενομοθέτηται. Ἐνταῦθα τὸν
Χριστὸν ἄντικρυς εἴρηκε βασιλέα· ὁ γὰρ τοῦτον διὰ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν παροξύνων,
ἁμαρτάνει εἰς τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ψυχήν. Ὥσπερ ὁ ἄφρων τὸ ὄνειδος οὐκ αἰσχύνεται, οὕτως
ὁ δανεισάμενος σῖτον σπεῖραι ἐν ἀμητῷ· ἤδη ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ γεωργίου αὐτοῦ
ἀποδοθήσεται τῷ δανείσαντι, κἂν τύχῃ ἀποθανεῖν τὸν δανεισθέντα. –Εἰ ἔστιν ἐν ἀμη
τῷ σῖτον δανείσασθαι παρὰ τῶν ἐργασαμένων ἐν τοῖς ἒξ ἔτεσι τὴν ἑαυτῶν γῆν,
τουτέστι παρὰ τῶν τῆς πρὸ τοῦ Χριστοῦ παρουσίας ἐν τοῖς ἒξ αἰῶσι λαμψάντων
δικαίων καὶ προφητῶν τὰς ἀρετὰς μιμήσασθαι, τῶν καὶ τρεφόντων ἐν τῷ ἑβδόμῳ
ἔτει χήραν καὶ ὀρφα νοὺς, εἰς τὸ ἀνταποδοθῆναι αὐτοῖς ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν
τὸν μισθὸν τῆς ἐνδείξεως τῶν ἀρετῶν, ὡς ἀπαρχὴ γεγονότες
pass_a_gloss: Wine makes anger unrestrained, leading people to excess; wrath is arrogant, born from heated passion. Since Nazirites avoid wine by law, they are thereby placed outside the realm of anger. Christ is directly named a king: whoever aggravates him through sin harms their own soul. Like the shameless fool unbothered by insult, so the lender of seed for barren soil expects repayment from the farm, even if the debtor dies. If one may borrow grain in fallow fields from those who cultivated their plots for six years—namely, the righteous and prophets who shone in the six eras before Christ—to emulate their deeds, including caring for widows and orphans in the sabbath year, then in heaven’s kingdom they will receive reward for displaying virtue, as first fruits of goodness. Those truly begotten through virtue will leave an icon 17.212 and blessing to posterity, and the blameless will impart nurturing righteousness to the end. Elsewhere it is said the slanderer falls silent; but Christ too: the one who abuses the Church loses faith, once their light before deceit; they may speak of outer darkness; thus it is declared for what is to come: and Christ can be called father and mother—father to those endowed with adoptive Spirit, mother to those craving milk, not solid nourishment. Christ speaking through Paul acted as father to Ephesians by unveiling wisdom’s secrets, as mother to Corinthians by feeding them milk. Sinful pleasure, called a first-portion reward, first sweetens the throat but later tastes worse than bile. Don’t boast in pride: “I fight my foes alone.” Instead, wait on and invoke the Lord for aid—don’t trust self-sufficiency, since David declares no help exists apart from God: “I don’t rely on my bow.” In physical matters, we name large and small weights: metals like gold, silver, bronze, lead, and all weighed items. Measures are things gauged in containers: grain, wine, oil, beans. Also, the one deemed rash yet timid by others is a large and small weight. Overall, every excess and deficit is a large and small weight—both are sins, and measures are twofold. Likewise, who wants to endure harm from others but won’t reciprocally ease others’ pain holds double measures—specifically, ignoring the rule: “Do unto others as you’d have them do unto you.” Not the poorly hearing ear, nor the poorly seeing eye, is God’s work; rather, the ear attending to good, and the eye beholding and envisioning the divine, are His work. One who listens to the Lord and keeps his laws does the Lord’s work; this holds for every bodily member. Use this against accusers who claim our body and God within us act arrogantly: stay awake, avoid oversleeping to escape Gehenna, refrain from slander. Let virtues open your soul’s eyes; let wisdom fill you with heavenly food. Balancing your life between the Lord’s deeds and 17.213 of the devil’s acts is detestable to God. The Lord names the mind a scale—innately just in judging events, yet swayed by self-interest via friends or wealth. Do not rush toward God’s vow, lest need or greed trigger repentance that insults Him by choosing another. Repentance over blessings comes not to the righteous but the wicked; the wicked must not vow to God without thought, since prayer invites repentance. —Quickly vowing to the Lord to sanctify your own, then swiftly reversing, traps the man. Christ winnows the impious: He assaults them like a lion seizing prey, or a fan tossing chaff from grain.
pass_b_english:
Wine, therefore, the unrestrained anger is; making men unrestrained; and wrath is insolent: for it arises from boiling anger. But if, according to the law, the Nazirites abstain from wine, then it has been ordained by law that the Nazirites are to be outside anger. Here Christ is plainly called a king: for the one who provokes him through sins, sins against his own soul. Just as the foolish man is not ashamed of disgrace, so the one who borrows grain to sow in an unplowed field: already, because it will be repaid from his farm to the lender, even if the borrower should happen to die. — If it is possible to borrow grain in an unplowed field from those who have worked their own land in the six years, that is, from those righteous ones and prophets who shone in the six ages before Christ’s presence, to imitate their virtues, those who also nourish in the seventh year the widow and the orphan, in order to repay them in the kingdom of heaven the reward of the manifestation of virtues, having become firstfruits of the virtues. Those whom, clearly by virtue, someone has begotten, will leave to those who come after an icon 17.212 and a blessing; and the unblemished one will leave righteousness of nurture until the end. For elsewhere it was said that the one who speaks evil ceases; but also Christ: and the one who reviles the Church will be deprived of the faith, which was to him light before the slander; and he would also speak concerning the outer darkness; therefore it has been said concerning the future: and Christ himself, father and mother, is able to be spoken of: father indeed of those who have the Spirit of adoption; mother however of those who need milk and not solid food.

And indeed, the Christ who speaks in Paul—though He is the one speaking—was made a father to the Ephesians, revealing to them the mysteries of wisdom; and He became a mother to the Corinthians, nourishing them with milk. The pleasure discovered among us that comes from evil, which he says is assigned as a portion in the first things, at first delights your palate, but later you will find it more bitter than gall. Do not speak, moved by pride: “I alone will wage war against my enemies”; but wait for the Lord and call upon Him, that He may help you. Do not rely on yourself as if you could act without the Lord; for He says through David that apart from Him there is no helper: “I do not trust in my bow.” Regarding sensible things, we say that a large and small weight exists—among which are gold, silver, bronze, lead, and whatever else is weighed. Measures, however, are those things measured in vessels: grain, wine, oil, and legumes. Furthermore, the person called bold yet timid by some, I consider to be a large and small weight. Moreover, universally, every excess and deficiency—this is a large and small weight; for both are vices, and measures are doubled. Furthermore, the one who wishes to suffer well at the hands of others, yet himself does not choose to similarly relieve others, possesses double measures—namely, not obeying the command that says: “Whatever you wish that people would do to you, you also do to them.” Not the ear that hears badly is the work of the Lord, but the one who attends to good things; and not the eye that sees badly is the work of the Lord, but the one who sees and imagines divine things.

For whoever hears the Lord and observes his commandments performs the work of the Lord. The same principle applies to all parts of the body. You should employ this statement against those who accuse us, saying that our body and the God within us are engaging in insolence. This means: do not sleep excessively, but remain wakeful, so that you may not be cast into Gehenna. Do not slander. Through the virtues, open the eyes of your soul. Through wisdom, be filled with heavenly bread. To weigh oneself against the works of the Lord and also 17.213 of the devil’s works is an abomination to the Lord. Yet the Lord calls a balance-scale the mind, which is naturally endowed to judge rightly the things that occur, but which is inclined by the impulse of self-will through friends or riches. Do not hasten, he says, toward the promise before God, lest the need, or the desire of the greater abundance, seize you and begin to repent, and you insult God by preferring something else to him. For repentance upon good things does not happen to the just, but to the unjust. The unjust, therefore, should not make any promise to God without careful consideration, for after praying, repentance arises. –To hastily dedicate oneself to the Lord, which is to sanctify something of one’s own, and then immediately afterward to change one’s mind, is a snare to the man. Christ is the winnower of the godless. He will come upon the godless like a lion upon prey. Or a winnowing fan, which separates the chaff from the grain, he will apply to them.
